interpretation: M1 (HIGH confidence; T1-F1/T1-F2 are exact, not statistical): 'all ordered fidelity pairs' is NOT data amplification on this family. After B2's target-indexed condition correction the cross rows carry no (X, Y) information the self rows do not already carry; their entire effect on the loss is to reweight the ladder by (1 + #levels below), i.e. to move effective weight AWAY from the only level with many distinct conditions TOWARD the level with five. `self_only` does not drop information - it removes a replication schedule that inverts the information ordering of the ladder. This re-scopes the s1 line: the largest single ifc_poisson lever found in this stream so far is row-set hygiene, not a modelling mechanism.

M2 (HIGH confidence; T2-F1 + T2-F4 are two-sided): the MF composition this card claims is real and is exactly a factorization of the calibration law into a level-LOCAL intercept and a level-TRANSFERABLE slope. The auxiliary levels are needed only for the 5-parameter direction; the 5 HF rows are exactly sufficient for the 1-parameter offset and useless for the direction. Evidence on both sides: intercept-only can never beat the control (best over all a with the slope off = the control), and transferring the aux intercept costs 3.2 floors.

M3 (HIGH confidence; T2-F3): the composition is not an 'aux data volume' effect - a 20-row auxiliary level reproduces the whole effect, and the 170-row pooled-aux slope is mid-pack. What transfers is a direction in condition space dominated by one coordinate (coord4, 75.6 % of the design variance). Practically the head is close to a one-coordinate amplitude law, which is also why it is cheap to estimate and why it is fragile to the base it is fitted on.

M4 (MODERATE-HIGH confidence; T2-F5) - CORRECTS a part-5 caveat: part 5 recorded that the measured F1 effect is 'plausibly a LOWER BOUND on what a de-attenuated law could deliver'. Quantified: that slack is 0.045x the noise floor (right sign, immaterial), because the attenuation is mostly genuine regression-to-the-mean rather than a fixable bias. The material residual is the 0.236-floor gap to the per-sample oracle, which is gain SHAPE that is not linear in the 5-D condition vector.

M5 (HIGH for the channel claim, MODERATE for the s5 delta; T3-F1/T3-F2): s5-B2's zscore target scaler and s1-B3's gain head are the SAME AXIS with different instruments - both act on the per-sample LEVEL (DC) channel of a 69 %-DC dataset (zscore at training time by removing the level from the target; the head post-hoc by rescaling it). The round report must NOT count them as two stackable ifc_poisson levers: after the s1 head the level rel-err (0.00879) is already below the s5 zscore arm's (0.01149). The only measured component off that axis is self_only's pattern-channel gain (-23 %), which no target-scaling lever in either stream produced. Caveat: s5's maxabs comparator at 200 epochs is s5-B1's own arm, not a knob-controlled A0 (which exists only at contract tier), so the s5 DELTA is directional; the per-arm channel SHARES are controlled facts on bit-identical targets.

M6 (MODERATE-HIGH confidence; T3-F3 + T1-F5): the effective-N reading of the self_only win. A level's information about an unseen HF condition is set by how densely it covers condition space, and the field SHAPE is almost perfectly shared across levels (r >= 0.95 after one gain), so the 100 level-8 rows are the ladder's real information about the 128 test conditions - a 1.61x better training-free HF predictor than the 5 HF rows, which are themselves barely better than the HF-train-mean predictor. allpairs reweights that information down 0.625x and replicates the 5 HF conditions 4x; the measured consequence is a larger condition-dependent amplitude error and a worse pattern. NOT isolated: a 1.64x gradient-step difference (18 vs 11 steps/epoch) rides along with the reweighting and cannot be separated without a training run, which is out of scope for this role.

M7 (MODERATE confidence; T1-F4/T1-F5 + T3-F2): stacking the head on a clean base is contraindicated, not neutral. The head is a patch for a defect that the allpairs row set creates; on a base without that defect it over-corrects by 4.5x in dispersion and costs 1.6 floors. Any batch-4 design that keeps both must re-fit the head on the base it will run on AND gate it on a measured dispersion check (e.g. std(log g_hat) / std(log g) on TRAIN aux rows) rather than assuming additivity.
6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: Both clauses were CONFIRMED and the mechanism is now identified rather than merely observed. F1 (the level-64 gain law is estimable from the auxiliary levels) held because the law's SLOPE - a direction in condition space, dominated by one coordinate - is genuinely shared across levels (per-level slope cosines 0.951-0.985; any single aux level, even a 20-row one, reproduces the effect to within 0.14x the noise floor), while the part of the law that is NOT shared, the intercept, is the one parameter the 5 HF rows can actually estimate. The brainstormer's modal call ('F1 FALSIFIED') came from a co-kriging prior that per-level parameter estimates differ; that prior is right about the intercept (aux -0.0604/-0.0590/-0.0481 vs HF -0.0021, 5.37 pp apart, exactly the pre-registered >>3 % rule) and wrong about the slope - and the card's estimator happened to split the law along precisely that seam, which is why it worked. F2 was confirmed only in the weak sense part 5 already flagged: gain__hf_only is a numerical no-op (g_hat 1.0000079 +/- 5.49e-05) because stage 2 finetunes 200 epochs on the 5 HF rows and the base reproduces them (in-sample level-64 log-g std 0.000936, train rel-L2 0.004815), so there is no signal to fit; F2 is F1 re-run against a comparator that did nothing, and the composition claim rests on F1 plus the per-level coefficient table, not on F2. The thin margins remain thin: F1 clears by 1.076x the floor on ONE seed, and turn 2 shows the honest ceiling for this head (intercept + dispersion both fitted on test) is only 0.045x the floor above what was measured - so the confirmation pass will be deciding a 1.08x-floor effect, not a comfortable one.
surprises: The card's biggest number came from the arm with no mechanism in it, and the mechanism turns out to be a bookkeeping artifact: allpairs' 105 'extra' rows are exact duplicates (175 distinct (X,Y) rows out of 280). The all-ordered-pairs augmentation that has been carried since B1 was, after B2's own correction, only a per-level replication schedule.

The gain head and the self_only row set fix the SAME per-sample channel (per-sample improvement corr 0.929), so the two headline results of this card are largely non-additive - and stacking them is actively harmful (0.021913 -> 0.035890), which no part of the design anticipated.
A 20-row auxiliary level supplies a better slope than the 170-row pooled fit (0.024791 vs 0.024977). More auxiliary supervision is not better supervision here.
The under-dispersion flagged in part 5 as a possible lower-bound story is worth only 0.045x the noise floor once quantified, and the naive de-attenuation (k = 1/0.741) makes the arm WORSE.

Two thirds of ifc_poisson's field energy (0.6928) is the per-sample spatial mean, and every ifc_poisson gain measured in round 1 so far - s1's per-level scaler, s1's gain head, s5's zscore scaler - is a different instrument aimed at that same scalar. The only measured improvement to the actual pattern came from the self_only row set.

7_gap_and_future.open_question: Is the `self_only` win a CONDITION-COVERAGE (effective-N) effect or an OPTIMIZATION-BUDGET effect? Turn 1 proved the two row sets contain the same 175 distinct (X, Y) rows and differ only in a per-level replication schedule (x1/x2/x3/x4), which simultaneously (a) shifts effective loss weight 0.625x away from the 100-condition level and 2.5x toward the 5-condition HF level and (b) raises stage-1 gradient steps/epoch from 11 to 18.
